tough.h2: Built for a dog who is mostly zoomies and gas
tough.html:
Anyone who owns a Boston knows the routine. The tuxedo makes them look like they are headed to a wedding, and then they clear the room with one toot and fall asleep snoring on your pillow. That big round head leaves very little room for polite behavior.

A Boston never runs at one speed. It is nap, nap, nap, then thirty seconds of couch-surfing zoomies, then nap again. The tag takes all of that, so it gets laser engraved into the metal. Nothing to peel off when they skid into the coffee table.

Those bug eyes also mean a lot of face-first adventures, so the name and number go on the back where they stay readable.

How engraving holds up →

more.h2: Made by a house with seven bulldogs
more.lead: We're a family in Lehi, Utah with seven English bulldogs and one very busy laser. Boston Terriers and English bulldogs share a love of blankets, a snoring habit and a gas problem we will not discuss. We wrote the bulldog tags first, from experience, and the Boston lines come from friends whose tuxedo dogs sleep on their heads.

items.q: Will mud, drool and rough play wear off the engraving?
items.a: No. The text is laser engraved into the metal, so scuffing doesn't erase it.

items.q: Can I put my Boston's name and my phone number on the tag?
items.a: Yes. Saying on the front, name and phone number on the back.

items.q: Do you have sayings written specifically for Bostons?
items.a: 12 on this page. Each fits the tag as written.

items.q: What should I put on a Boston Terrier's tag?
items.a: Pick one joke for the front and keep it under two short lines, like Tuxedo on. Manners off. Put your dog's name and a phone number on the back. Skip anything cutesy that hides the number.

items.q: What happens if the engraving comes out wrong?
items.a: If we mis-engrave it, we remake it free. Tags are engraved and shipped from Lehi, Utah in 1 to 2 business days, then USPS takes 3 to 5 days in transit. US only.
